title: NVIDIA Debloated Driver (clean-room build)
description: Builds a debloated NVIDIA display driver and prepares it for offline injection into a Tiny11 Core-Gaming ISO. This is a clean-room implementation: it downloads the official NVIDIA DCH package, prunes it to the Display Driver, applies the registry tweaks as INF AddReg edits and re-signs the result. It does not use, bundle or drive NVCleanstall, and it contains no third-party code. The debloating approach is inspired by TechPowerUp's NVCleanstall.
author: kelexine (https://github.com/kelexine)

resolver.note: Templates are tried in order, then each branch candidate, until one returns a package larger than minPackageBytes (100 MB). A real driver package is several hundred MB; anything smaller is an error page, not a driver.

components.note: Pruning is allowlist-based: only the folders in keepFolders survive. The remove list documents the components that are dropped and matches the reference component selection exactly. Display Driver is the only component that must stay. displayInfGlob selects the INFs to tweak: a DCH package splits devices across dozens of self-contained display INFs (nv_dispi.inf, nvami.inf, nvbli.inf, nvdmi.inf, nvlti.inf, ...), one per GPU family, so the tweaks must be applied to all of them or most GPUs would keep the untouched driver.

tweaks.note: These are the tweaks that translate into registry state on the target machine. They are written as INF AddReg lines and wired into every DDInstall section, so Windows applies them when it installs the driver. Install-time-only tweaks (unattended express install, clean install, auto-accept unsigned warning) have no offline INF equivalent and are handled by the first-boot installer instead.

addReg.description: Enable Message Signaled Interrupts and raise the device interrupt priority, which reduces DPC latency.
Stop the driver from reporting usage telemetry.
Disable the HD Audio sleep timer so the audio endpoint does not power down mid-session.
Zero the HDCP key so the display link does not enforce HDCP.

signing.subject: CN=Tiny11 NVIDIA Driver Rebuild
signing.note: Editing the INF invalidates NVIDIA's catalog, so a tweaked driver will not install from the DriverStore unless it is re-signed. inf2cat.exe (Windows Driver Kit) rebuilds the catalog and signtool.exe (Windows SDK) signs it with a locally generated certificate. If either tool is missing, the builder skips the INF tweaks and ships the pristine NVIDIA-signed driver instead, so the output always installs.

injection.note: The driver is added to the offline install.wim DriverStore before WinSxS optimization, so PnP installs it during OOBE. Because a re-signed driver's catalog is not NVIDIA's, the certificate is also trusted inside the image and a first-boot installer runs from SetupComplete.cmd as a guaranteed fallback.
